questionText: A cache memory unit with capacity of $N$ words and block size of $B$ words is to be designed. If it is designed as a direct mapped cache, the length of the TAG field is 10 bits. If the cache unit is now designed as a 16-way set-associative cache, the length of the TAG field is _________ bits.
explanation:
Step 1: Determine total number of blocks
Total cache capacity = $N$ words
Block size = $B$ words
Total number of blocks in cache = $N / B$

Step 2: Direct Mapped Cache Analysis
In a direct-mapped cache:
- Word offset bits = $\log_2 B$
- Line index bits = $\log_2 (N / B) = \log_2 N - \log_2 B$
- TAG field = $10$ bits

Total Main Memory Address Bits = $\text{TAG} + \text{Index} + \text{Offset}$
$\text{Address Bits} = 10 + (\log_2 N - \log_2 B) + \log_2 B = 10 + \log_2 N$

Step 3: 16-Way Set-Associative Cache Analysis
In a 16-way set-associative cache:
- Number of sets = $(N / B) / 16 = N / (16B)$
- Set index bits = $\log_2 (N / (16B)) = \log_2 N - \log_2 B - 4$
- Word offset bits = $\log_2 B$

Since the total main memory address length remains unchanged:
$\text{TAG}_{16\text{-way}} + \text{Set Index Bits} + \text{Offset Bits} = 10 + \log_2 N$
$\text{TAG}_{16\text{-way}} + (\log_2 N - \log_2 B - 4) + \log_2 B = 10 + \log_2 N$
$\text{TAG}_{16\text{-way}} - 4 = 10$
$\text{TAG}_{16\text{-way}} = 14$ bits.

Final Answer:
14
